implementation_notes: The document is a C struct whose fields are copied to and from a wire buffer explicitly: fix field order and widths, convert 16/32-bit integers with htons/htonl and ntohs/ntohl from <arpa/inet.h>, prefix the body with a length and a version, and never memcpy a struct image onto the wire because padding and endianness differ per target. Ownership is part of the contract - the decoder allocates the document, the receiver frees it on exactly one path - and every length read from the wire is validated before it indexes or allocates. This is the default C realization because it works with no dependencies and keeps payload sizes minimal on embedded and high-volume paths; where the document is already JSON, cJSON's cJSON_Parse/cJSON_Print tree is the usual shortcut.
pitfalls: Every wire-derived length must be bounded before it is used for allocation or indexing; the classic document-parser bug is a heap overflow behind a plausible header.
One owner per document, freed exactly once: half-finished decode paths leak, and a borrowed pointer into a message buffer dangles after that buffer is reused.
Struct padding and alignment make the in-memory layout unusable as a wire format; without htonl/ntohl the same code passes on x86 and corrupts data on a big-endian target.

variants.name: protobuf-c generated documents
variants.implementation_notes: When the document contract is shared with other languages, the schema lives in a .proto file and protoc --c_out (the protoc-gen-c plugin) generates .pb-c.c/.pb-c.h with a descriptor per message; you pack with protobuf_c_message_pack/pack_to_buffer and unpack with protobuf_c_message_unpack, then free with protobuf_c_message_free_unpacked. The generated headers are not standalone artifacts - they carry version guards against the installed libprotobuf-c - so they must be regenerated as part of the build rather than vendored. Choose this route when field evolution and cross-language contracts outweigh the dependency and codegen cost.
pitfalls: Generated .pb-c.h files must be rebuilt with the same libprotobuf-c version they are compiled against; vendoring them produces version-guard failures or silent ABI skew.
protobuf_c_message_unpack allocates the whole document, so the receiver owns the free - forgetting protobuf_c_message_free_unpacked leaks on every message.
The protoc/protoc-gen-c toolchain becomes a hard build dependency and must be pinned, or the document contract drifts between developers and CI.
